questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university profile and reputation. The language spoken in the country. The city being a decently interesting city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy regarding most of the formal stuff. Social activities and knowledge thereof were sparse.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a meeting of about an hour with a guide to choosing courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
Not a very welcoming experience. The university should facilitate some chances for the exchange students in the institute/faculty to meet each other. It doesn't have to be anything fancy or formal. Just coordinate a meeting between the exchange student studying the same as each other and maybe sponsor a pizza or whatever.

Maybe a quick showing of campus could be handy, too. Or an introduction to social events being hosted by students (also locals) within the faculty/institute.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult. Write to a lot of people - preferably in German as it provides you with a lot more answers. WG-Gesucht gave the most results, and I'd say it's worth it to invest in WG-Gesucht + (or pro or whatever it is called).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is good but can be difficult late during week nights. Would recommend a 'Deutschlandsticket'.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's not the university's fault that the housing market is tough in Munich, and I actually think that they were quite helpful in every area where it was possible for them to be of any help.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Most of it was explained quite thoroughly in emails leading up to the stay. I had no issues just following the instructions there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Thorough emails

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Following the instructions meticulously. The international office is quick to repsond if any questions are sent their way.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Courses were generally easier than in Copenhagen but still pretty good. Germans start a little earlier at university so I would recommend picking seminars for later bachelor og master semesters.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar - pretty much the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Habermas
Krieg und Gewalt in der politischen Philosophie
The European Union in Complex Policy Areas
Democratic Development and Stability in Germany
Debates in Democracy Research

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Master courses are good, but you need a special permit from the responsible professors if you're still a bachelors student. The seminars in the philosophy department that I had were really good!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They offered close to nothing. Everything social was outside the university (ESN MESA, for instance).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As stated above, barely any. There was one Christmas party at the Institute of Political Science, but other than that none - not any that were of relevance to me at least.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to ESN MESA. They have an incredible amount of acitivities where you can always meet someone.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Exploit the fact that Munich is located so centrally in Europe. Go to cities in Central Europe by train. Often times it takes no longer than four hours to reach great cities.

Other than that, Munich is a pretty city. Go visit some of the older parts in the city center and explore the area around the Isar - especially Glockenbach and Gärtnerplatzviertel.

Join the day trips to cities and the Alps that ESN MESA organizes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Quite easy. I had some worries about the hierarchical, very formal structure of German Universities, but it turned out to be rather chill. The professors were all kind and approachable.

Other than that, there are mainly minor differences between Denmark and Germany. Engage with locals and you'll learn them quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take German courses and engage with the students there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Politeness, openness (compared to DK), and political awareness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Start looking for a place to live early.

Practice your German before and during your stay.

Go to ESN MESA.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have any administrative hindrances that you'd like to overcome - for instance regarding access to a course or whatever - talk to the relevant professor. They have a lot more 'power' in deciding administrative stuff regarding their own courses than professors in Denmark have.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Probably the language part - and of course, some acquaintances too.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being quite isolated for the first three weeks or so, and having to do the work of making new social acquaintances.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
